matching_bullets: A self-replicating npm worm takes over the keyv caching packages and leaves a start-up hook inside developers' agent configuration
verifications.reason: The npm worm is a textbook entry against the rubric's generic list: supply-chain attack, credential and token exfiltration, agent hijack. An account takeover of the keyv maintainer drove poisoned releases through the repository's own GitHub Actions workflow, so the compromised versions carried valid provenance signatures — the artefact an auditor checks to conclude a package is clean. Aikido counted at least 868 packages across 1,381 versions, the preinstall payload sweeps npm, GitHub, OIDC, AWS, Kubernetes, Vault, Stripe, Slack, SSH, Docker and Terraform secrets, and it self-republishes through any publish token it finds. The events bullets add the AI-security track (Black Hat AI Summit, BSides Las Vegas [un]prompted, DEF CON AI Village).

No CVE identifier, no CVSS score and no severity-rated advisory anywhere in the file; a self-anchored scan returns zero CVE-YYYY-N and zero CVSS hits. Judged against the rubric rather than by adjacency: today's npm worm is an active supply-chain incident driven by credential theft and a malicious publish, not a vulnerability disclosure with a scored CVE, so it belongs to AI Security and does not satisfy this topic.
